name: Quantule Mapper Colab Capsule Workflow
purpose: Use Google Colab as a burst-compute lane for targeted, preregistered simulations and cross-hardware checks.
not_for: jobs that cannot persist useful partial results
jobs expected to exceed Colab session limits

result_policy.notes: Keep returned archives below 1 GB when practical. The generated notebook refuses to copy archives over 5 GB.

resource_profile_defaults.notes: The packager applies runtime resource policy and profiling. Larger T/grid/box/row counts must be explicit in the run queue and manifest arguments.

control_panel.safety_boundary: Dashboard statuses report infrastructure state only. They do not validate scientific claims.

workflow.description: Choose a small, targeted simulation with a clear single entrypoint or manifest-declared row stages, arguments, source allowlist, expected outputs, and Drive result directory.

Prompt the agent to use notebook_packager_v4.py and provide or approve a suitable JSON manifest. Future agents should only need to write the manifest when all simulation and analysis scripts already exist.
Run the packager locally against the project root and manifest. Verify dry-run hash output and notebook cell compilation.
Upload the generated .ipynb to Google Colab manually and select the intended GPU runtime.
Run notebook cells top to bottom in Colab. The notebook extracts files, verifies hashes, performs preflight checks, executes the job, and archives results.
Copy the result archive to the manifest drive_results_dir when the archive is under the hard size cap.
Download the archive from Drive and place it in F:\quantule_mapper\colab_jobs\results.
Review the downloaded result capsule, compare outputs against expected files and gates, then resume the normal local workflow.

required_manifest_fields: queue colab push target for colab-a100 rows
agent_control_panel_rules: T1, T2 and T3 are immutable reserved slots.
Every action must name exactly one output_channel.
Job actions must reference a declared row_id or job subset.
The UI may invoke only registered trusted handlers.
Full logs must be persisted outside the widget.
Agents should use control_panel_ui_bridge.json or the stable runtime handle registries instead of scraping notebook output.
Buttons do not constitute completion evidence; status files and hashes do.
A regenerated capsule must produce the same action routing for the same canonical manifest.

manifest_only_staged_row_contract.purpose: Allow an agent to create a Colab capsule by writing one JSON manifest when the underlying simulation and analysis scripts already exist.

rows[].stages[].stage_id: stable short identifier such as simulation or analysis
arguments: literal argv values; strings may use {job_root}, {job_id}, {row_id}, and {stage_id}
expected_outputs: job-root-relative files that must exist after this stage

runtime_behavior: The J-button runs stages sequentially in the declared order.
All stage stdout/stderr streams into the action's dedicated output terminal and persistent log.
Stage expected_outputs are fail-closed before the next stage runs.
The row is committed only after all stages complete and row-level expected_outputs pass.
The final archive still includes provenance, control-panel logs, status files, and integrity hashes.
limits: The packager does not invent analysis logic or scientific tolerances.
Custom comparison logic still belongs in an existing analysis script referenced by the manifest.
This remains a manual Colab upload lane, not a dynamic orchestration service.

runtime_environment_contract.purpose: Let a manifest override runtime controls, such as JAX/XLA memory allocation settings, without editing packaged scientific source files.
runtime_behavior: The generated runtime setup cell applies these variables before any JAX import.
Child simulation and analysis subprocesses inherit the same environment.
Scripts that use os.environ.setdefault keep the manifest value.
The applied values are recorded in runtime_environment_overrides.json.
limits: This changes execution environment policy only; it must not be used to alter scientific equations or validation gates.
Higher memory fractions can improve A100 utilization but may increase out-of-memory risk.

resource_profile_contract.purpose: Make Colab resource policy and utilization evidence a manifest-level contract without editing scientific source files.
runtime_behavior: The packager resolves defaults and exposes RESOURCE_PROFILE in the generated notebook.
The runtime setup cell applies XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE and XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION before JAX imports.
T1 records CPU RAM, disk, GPU memory, GPU utilization, JAX backend, device list and x64 status.
T2 runs a bounded generic JAX float64 resource probe and writes it into the smoke-test artifact.
The final archive provenance includes the resolved resource profile.
limits: The resource profile does not automatically alter scientific arguments.
If Colab should push a longer T, larger grid, larger box, denser cadence, or batched physics path, the queue's colab push target and manifest arguments must say so.
Low GPU memory use is not automatically a defect; inspect utilization and logs before changing scientific scale.
Independent jobs may use separate Colab tabs/sessions rather than being bundled into one capsule.

analogy: Sometimes it is quicker to send the car to the shop than fix it yourself.
